topic: Complete removable-root calibration frontier for paired Gaussian LiMVAMs. For finite p variables and m views, observe every within-view covariance but paired cross-view blocks only inside a calibration subset S; views share an unknown topological order, view-specific coefficients, and independent-across-variable Gaussian disturbance vectors with positive-definite cross-view covariances. Prove that an order is compatible iff its order-constrained modified-Cholesky residual cross-blocks are diagonal, and that a removable-root recursion is necessary and sufficient with Schur-complement state indexed only by the removed variable set. Build a memoized 2^p-state plus output-size algorithm returning all distinct full-view coefficient tuples, positive-definite noise certificates, the essential ancestral poset, and a minimum-cardinality S identifying the full tuple. Add finite-sample operator-norm covariance-region inversion, Hausdorff coefficient-set consistency off feasibility boundaries, and exact poset recovery under fixed score and path-product margins. Apply it to Heurtebise et al.'s Cam-CAN MEG and fMRI PairwiseLiMVAM/DirectLiMVAM workflow, using a certified participant calibration subset for order while retaining every participant marginal for coefficients.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the complete observational-equivalence class of shared-order Gaussian LiMVAM coefficient tuples when every within-view covariance is observed but cross-view covariance blocks are observed only among a calibration subset of views.

source_refs.claim: LiMVAM uses correlation across jointly sampled views to identify acyclic linear SEMs without non-Gaussian disturbances, but does not give an equivalence frontier when only a strict subset of cross-view blocks is observed.
source_refs.author: Ambroise Heurtebise, Omar Chehab, Pierre Ablin, Alexandre Gramfort, Aapo Hyvärinen

source_refs.claim: Integrates second-order information from experiments with overlapping measured-variable sets and characterizes what is determined, but uses neither paired views nor view-specific coefficient matrices under a shared order.
source_refs.author: Antti Hyttinen, Frederick Eberhardt, Patrik O. Hoyer

open_problems.why_unsolved: Heurtebise et al. explicitly define multi-view data through paired observations and use the resulting full cross-view correlation system in recursive-residual and joint-diagonalization arguments. Deleting cross-view blocks removes order-dependent disturbance-orthogonality equations, while the overlapping-dataset literature allows different measured variables or experiments but not the present combination of view-specific coefficients, one shared unknown order, Gaussian disturbances, and a selected cross-block pattern. The first proof step that must change is the global full-pairing identifiability argument: it must be replaced by an orderwise modified-Cholesky residual criterion and a proof that sequential projection is path-independent because its Schur complement depends only on the removed set.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if compatibility theorem based on diagonal selected residual cross-blocks, together with a necessary-and-sufficient removed-set Schur recursion that characterizes every compatible coefficient tuple, positive-definite disturbance completion, and invariant ancestral relation.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from Gaussian single-view nonidentifiability to cross-view information and shared-order recovery, while making partial calibration the new data constraint.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Gaussian linear SEMs are not direction-identifiable from one covariance -> paired views carry cross-view disturbance information -> only some views may be jointly calibrated -> characterize exactly which orders and coefficients remain compatible

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the paper's cross-covariance root criterion and shared-order recursive residualization, proving necessity and sufficiency after retaining only the selected cross-block equations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the source model and already turns cross-view disturbance structure into causal-order information; the new proof must show exactly what survives deletion of unobserved blocks.

method_exemplars.technique: Port recursive extremal-vertex removal, Schur-complement updating, and finite-sample propagation of covariance or precision-matrix errors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems recurse by deleting a certified vertex and updating a second-moment state; LiMVAM replaces the sink criterion by selected residual cross-orthogonality.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop an output-sensitive quotient enumeration algorithm that emits every distinct full-view LiMVAM coefficient tuple exactly once from the removed-set order DAG without traversing all compatible topological orders.

source_refs.claim: Recursively enumerates subclasses on which a total-effect functional is distinct, eliminating duplicate causal-function outputs created by enumerating all compatible DAGs.
source_refs.author: F. Richard Guo, Emilija Perković

source_refs.claim: Gives linear-delay enumeration of all DAGs in a Markov equivalence class, but its outputs are graph-distinct DAGs rather than covariance-dependent classes with identical numerical coefficient tuples.
source_refs.author: Marcel Wienöbst, Malte Luttermann, Max Bannach, Maciej Liśkiewicz

source_refs.excerpt: Unconditional deterministic polynomial-delay generation of all vertices remains unresolved.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature solves either graph-distinct MEC enumeration or duplicate-free enumeration when a finite set of graphical orientations characterizes equality of the causal functional. The prior CausalSmith vertex-calculus run independently exposes the analogous failure point: a canonical parent map is insufficient when inverse children cannot be generated at degenerate states. LiMVAM tuple equality is more delicate because zero coefficients and commuting removable roots can make factorially many order paths yield one numerical tuple. The first proof step is to replace graphical orientation or active-basis signatures by a canonical full-view coefficient-and-noise signature, then prove a reachable parent map and locally generatable children on the quotient without first visiting every inducing order.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sound and complete algorithm with O(poly(p,m)2^p + poly(p,m)N_out) total time or polynomial delay, a proof of exact-once output for each distinct tuple, and a canonical inducing-order and positive-definite-noise certificate, or a matching impossibility result for the stated computation model.

writing_exemplar.why: Its problem formulation cleanly distinguishes enumerating structural representatives from minimally enumerating distinct causal-function outputs.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Structural ambiguity produces many compatible DAGs -> naive enumeration repeats causal quantities -> recursive subclassing removes functional duplicates -> quotient LiMVAM order paths by their full coefficient tuple

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the recursive partition into maximal subclasses on which an output functional is fixed, replacing effect-identifying orientations by tuple-preserving removable-root transitions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired output is likewise a minimal list of distinct causal functionals rather than all structural representatives.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its bounded-delay traversal and local transition analysis to canonical quotient states of the removed-set DAG.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest delay-sensitive causal-DAG enumeration machinery, while the new proof must establish reachability after numerical tuple merging.

method_exemplars.technique: Build an acyclic reverse-search parent relation with a reachable root and polynomially generatable local children, avoiding a global visited set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The unresolved object is precisely a parent-and-child structure on equivalence classes rather than raw permutations.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize and compute a minimum-cardinality subset of views whose paired cross-covariances identify the full tuple of all view-specific LiMVAM coefficients while the remaining views contribute only marginal covariances.

source_refs.claim: The shared-order LiMVAM result pools information across fully paired views but does not optimize which views must provide paired cross-covariances for recovery of every view-specific coefficient matrix.
source_refs.author: Ambroise Heurtebise, Omar Chehab, Pierre Ablin, Alexandre Gramfort, Aapo Hyvärinen

source_refs.claim: Produces in polynomial time a minimum intervention-target set guaranteeing full DAG identifiability, demonstrating how information acquisition can be posed as an exact minimum design problem.
source_refs.author: Alain Hauser, Peter Bühlmann

source_refs.claim: Proves NP-hardness and approximation guarantees for cost-aware intervention design, but its separating objects are interventional edge orientations rather than passive residual cross-covariance equations.
source_refs.author: Erik M. Lindgren, Murat Kocaoglu, Alexandros G. Dimakis, Sriram Vishwanath

source_refs.excerpt: Add a genuine design result: optimize the support-incidence frontier under a stated intervention-budget constraint

open_problems.why_unsolved: Intervention-design papers optimize chosen perturbations through graphical separation in an essential graph, while the prior BACKSHIFT review asks for a support-incidence design frontier across covariance regimes. LiMVAM calibration is passive and its information gain depends on numerical equality or inequality of candidate-order residual correlations. The first missing step is to associate every pair of coefficient-distinct compatible orders with the calibrated views whose residual cross-blocks separate them, prove that hitting every such witness set is equivalent to full-tuple identification, and handle witness collapse on equal-correlation or zero-edge strata. Ordinary set cover alone supplies neither that equivalence nor the correct complexity classification.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient residual-witness hitting-set characterization of identifying subsets S, with an exact minimum-cardinality algorithm and certificates for sufficiency and failure of every smaller subset, or an NP-hardness theorem with a proved approximation guarantee.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its argument that weak individual views borrow order information across paired measurements, then sharpen the motivation into the resource question of which views actually require paired acquisition.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Individual Gaussian views do not reveal direction -> paired views can identify a shared order -> pairing every view may be costly or unavailable -> find the smallest paired-view subset that identifies every coefficient matrix

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the reduction of full-identification design to a minimum family of separating targets and prove that every remaining ambiguity is hit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination also seeks a smallest measurement design separating every observationally compatible causal alternative, with passive covariance witnesses replacing interventions.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the cost-aware covering formulation, hardness reduction, and greedy approximation analysis to residual-correlation witnesses indexed by view subsets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the closest machinery if minimum calibration reduces to weighted hitting set.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer finite-sample Gaussian-DAG separation analysis to show when empirical residual witnesses preserve the population minimum calibration design and exact-order conclusion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both require distinguishing Gaussian structural alternatives from estimated second moments under an explicit signal margin.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct finite-sample covariance-region inversion for the calibration-subset LiMVAM identified set, with Hausdorff consistency away from feasibility collisions and exact essential-poset recovery under explicit residual-score and path-product margins.

source_refs.claim: Proves consistency of pairwise likelihood and cross-covariance criteria but does not invert an operator-norm covariance region into all compatible LiMVAM tuples or give exact ancestral-poset recovery margins.
source_refs.author: Ambroise Heurtebise, Omar Chehab, Pierre Ablin, Alexandre Gramfort, Aapo Hyvärinen

source_refs.claim: Develops sample-criterion inversion, Hausdorff-consistent estimation, rates, and confidence regions for identified sets.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, Elie Tamer

source_refs.claim: Proves finite-sample structure and coefficient recovery for a recursively reduced linear SEM under explicit separation and controlled covariance or precision estimation.
source_refs.author: Asish Ghoshal, Jean Honorio

source_refs.excerpt: Turn the certificate handle into an explicit semialgebraic decision procedure with input encoding, termination argument

open_problems.why_unsolved: The population feasible-set map changes discontinuously when an off-diagonal residual cross-covariance vanishes, two root scores tie, a path product vanishes, or a positive-definiteness boundary is reached, so pairwise pointwise consistency does not control the entire tuple set or poset. Generic set-inference theory does not by itself establish metric regularity for this order-stratified rational inverse image, and recursive Gaussian-SEM analyses assume a point-identified graph rather than controlling branch creation and deletion. The BACKSHIFT reviewer adds a computational obstruction: the feasibility oracle must be turned into an encoded terminating decision procedure, here after replacing affine simultaneous-diagonalization constraints by denominator-cleared modified-Cholesky residual equations and principal-minor inequalities.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An encoded covariance-region inversion algorithm with membership and emptiness certificates, honest finite-sample coverage, Hausdorff convergence of coefficient sets off stated feasibility boundaries, and high-probability exact ancestral-poset recovery under fixed residual-score and path-product margins.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its separation of identified-set estimation, Hausdorff control, and confidence-region construction instead of reporting a plug-in point estimate.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational restrictions define a parameter set -> sample analogues perturb its boundary -> pointwise consistency is insufficient for set coverage -> invert covariance uncertainty through the LiMVAM feasibility map

method_exemplars.technique: Use contour-set inversion of a sample feasibility criterion and metric separation to prove consistency, rates, and coverage for a non-singleton target.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The LiMVAM output is an identified set defined by equality and positive-definiteness restrictions, matching criterion-minimizer geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt nonasymptotic control of recursive Schur updates and margin-based vertex selection to simultaneous root decisions over every reachable removed-set state.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly analyzes how second-moment estimation error propagates through a recursive extremal-vertex SEM algorithm.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate concentration of empirical cross-covariances into explicit multi-view recovery error through a spectral perturbation argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is a recent multi-view example of converting operator-norm cross-covariance uncertainty and separation into finite-sample recovery guarantees.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine when a nonrandom participant calibration subset yields target-population cross-view covariances for LiMVAM order discovery in multimodal Cam-CAN analysis and characterize failure when calibration selection depends on the signals.

source_refs.claim: Documents Cam-CAN's modality-dependent MRI and MEG cohort and motivates integrative multimodal analysis, so availability of jointly usable participants is a substantive sampling issue.
source_refs.author: Jason R. Taylor, Nitin Williams, Rhodri Cusack, Tibor Auer, Meredith A. Shafto, Marie Dixon, Lorraine K. Tyler, Cam-CAN, Richard N. Henson

source_refs.claim: Gives graphical conditions and procedures for recoverability and testability under MAR and MNAR mechanisms, emphasizing that observed-case distributions need not equal target distributions.
source_refs.author: Karthika Mohan, Judea Pearl
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Builds the LiMVAM cross-covariance criterion from paired samples sharing a sample index, so its population target is not automatically preserved by preferential participant selection.
source_refs.author: Ambroise Heurtebise, Omar Chehab, Pierre Ablin, Alexandre Gramfort, Aapo Hyvärinen

open_problems.why_unsolved: LiMVAM order compatibility depends on exact cross-view residual covariances, but a covariance computed only among calibrated participants equals the target-population block only under an explicit selection or missingness restriction. Cam-CAN's modality-dependent availability makes representativeness an additional identification assumption. Missing-data theory characterizes recovery of distributions and many causal functionals, but the searched literature does not derive recovery of the particular residual-diagonality equations or prove that replacing their cross-blocks by selection-corrected versions preserves the removable-root compatibility frontier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A selection- or missingness-graph theorem giving necessary and sufficient conditions and an observed-data formula for each target cross-view covariance block used by the LiMVAM recursion, plus a failure counterexample and a proof that substituting recovered blocks preserves the compatible-order and coefficient-tuple set.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its multimodal-cohort motivation and accounting of modality-specific acquisition, then make calibration selection the obstacle to valid integrative causal analysis.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Cam-CAN offers rich MRI and MEG measurements -> integrative analysis can exploit shared participants and tasks -> usable paired calibration may be selected -> establish when its cross-view moments transport to the target participant collection

method_exemplars.technique: Apply missingness-graph recoverability and testability rules to express the required second moments using observed variables and selection indicators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination asks whether a specific probabilistic functional, not necessarily the full law, is recoverable from systematically incomplete paired observations.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a sample criterion built from recovered or weighted covariance blocks to form an honest confidence region for the compatible LiMVAM set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Even after selection correction, the causal output can remain a non-singleton set defined by equality restrictions.

literature_map:
Heurtebise et al. (ICML 2026, arXiv:2502.20115) is the central anchor: LiMVAM replaces non-Gaussianity with cross-view correlation/noise diversity, uses shared-order recursive residuals, and applies the methods to neuroimaging.
Richard et al. (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2110.13502) supplies Shared-ICA identification and joint-diagonalization machinery underlying the Gaussian multi-view argument.
Anderson et al. (IEEE TSP 2014, arXiv:1303.7474) gives foundational independent-vector-analysis identification conditions and performance bounds.
Shimizu (Neurocomputing 2012, arXiv:1104.5341) jointly estimates multiple LiNGAMs with a shared order but retains non-Gaussianity and does not use paired cross-view covariance.
Hyttinen, Eberhardt, and Hoyer (UAI 2012, arXiv:1210.4879) integrate second-order information from overlapping experiments under a different coefficient-sharing model.
Peters and Bühlmann (Biometrika 2014, arXiv:1205.2536) and Wu and Drton (IEEE JSAIT 2023, arXiv:2308.08959) show how variance restrictions refine Gaussian-DAG equivalence, motivating an explicit partial-calibration equivalence frontier.
Ghoshal and Honorio (AISTATS 2018, arXiv:1707.04673) is the closest recursive finite-sample analogue: extremal-vertex removal, Schur updates, separation margins, and coefficient-error control.
Gao, Tai, and Aragam (AISTATS 2022, arXiv:2201.10548) provides minimax sample-complexity benchmarks for Gaussian-DAG recovery under identifiable variance restrictions.
Guo and Perković (AISTATS 2021, arXiv:2010.08611) directly addresses minimal enumeration of distinct causal functionals and duplicate removal across compatible DAGs.
Wienöbst et al. (AAAI 2023, arXiv:2301.12212) gives linear-delay MEC enumeration, but not covariance-dependent quotient enumeration of coefficient tuples.
Hauser and Bühlmann (IJAR 2014, arXiv:1205.4174) and Lindgren et al. (NeurIPS 2018, arXiv:1810.11867) provide exact and cost-aware identification-design techniques whose passive-calibration analogue is unoccupied.
Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (Econometrica 2007, DOI 10.1111/j.1468-0262.2007.00794.x) is the natural identified-set inference anchor for covariance-region inversion and Hausdorff consistency.
Han, Matthes, and Shen (UAI 2026, arXiv:2602.23785) translates operator-norm cross-covariance concentration into multi-view recovery error through spectral perturbation.
Mohan and Pearl (JASA 2021, arXiv:1801.03583) shows why selected complete cases require recoverability conditions before their moments can be treated as population moments.
Taylor et al. (NeuroImage 2017, DOI 10.1016/j.neuroimage.2015.09.018) documents Cam-CAN's modality-dependent MRI/MEG cohort and motivates a certified, selection-aware participant-calibration analysis.
